title: Major wars in world history, 499 BC to AD 1988
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: A few wars show up again and again in history books, because they changed who ruled, where borders ran and how people lived afterward. Knowing their dates and sides gives the long story of the world a set of fixed points, from ancient Greece to the twentieth century.

How to hold it: Chunk by age: the ancient world (five wars, all BC), the Middle Ages (three), the early modern era (three), the 1800s (three) and the 1900s (six). Learn one age at a time and put the wars in order before learning the dates. For BC dates, remember that the numbers count down toward AD 1: the Greco-Persian Wars (499 BC) came before the Punic Wars (264 BC). Give each war a picture in its own room of a memory palace, and come back on day 1, 3, 7 and 21.
